h1: HOP INN Krung Thonburi Station — BTS right outside, clean rooms, budget price on Bangkok's Thonburi side
intro: If you want a Bangkok base where you step out the door and the BTS is already there — no Grab wait, no traffic gamble — HOP INN Bangkok Krung Thonburi Station delivers exactly that. BTS Krung Thonburi (Green Line Silom) is attached directly to the hotel entrance, a walk of under a minute. From that station you can be in Silom (Chong Nonsi) in two stops, at Saphan Taksin pier for river ferries in three, and the Gold Line BTS connects to ICONSIAM in 1.6 km without touching a taxi. Part of the Hop Inn chain under The Erawan Group, the hotel has 120 rooms from about ฿800/night, and a score of 9.1 from over 600 real guest reviews — an unusually strong result for this price tier.

body.html: Who this hotel is for — HOP INN Krung Thonburi Station is not selling luxury; it is selling a specific practical advantage that is genuinely hard to find at this price in Bangkok: a clean, budget room with a BTS station literally at the door. Travellers who get the most from it are business visitors who need a no-frills base with fast access to Silom and Sathon, tourists who want the West Thonburi experience (Talat Phlu street food, Wongwian Yai market, old-Bangkok neighbourhood feel) without paying Silom hotel prices, and ICONSIAM shoppers who prefer arriving by Gold Line BTS in minutes rather than fighting riverside traffic. The Thonburi side of the river here is authentic, lived-in Bangkok — not a tourist bubble — with morning markets, traditional shophouses, and the King Taksin Monument roundabout nearby. If you want a rooftop pool, a hotel gym, or breakfast served in a dining room, look at a pricier category. If you want the BTS, a clean bed, and honest value, this is one of Bangkok's stronger budget answers.

Location and getting around — the hotel stands at 89/1 Krung Thonburi Road, Khlong Ton Sai, Khlong San, Bangkok. BTS Krung Thonburi station is attached to the building — reviewers consistently say "30 seconds from the door". From here the Green Line (Silom) runs inbound: Chong Nonsi (Silom) is 1 stop, Chan Road/Sathon is 2 stops, Saphan Taksin (Chao Phraya pier) is 3 stops. The Gold Line BTS departs from Krung Thonburi station every 10–15 minutes to Klong San and ICONSIAM, fare ฿15–25, about 5–8 minutes. Free on-site parking is available for guests who drive — a real advantage on the Thonburi side where many visitors arrive by car. Food options directly around the hotel are limited (especially late at night), so expect to walk a few minutes onto Krung Thonburi Road or order via Grab Food.
"Location is unbeatable — the BTS station is right outside with a lift. Very nice and clean hotel. Good price too. The front desk staff were always smiling and very polite."

Rooms and facilities — 120 rooms in two main configurations: Standard Double (queen bed) and Standard Twin (two single beds), both approximately 18 sqm. Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a mini fridge, a work desk, and an en-suite shower room with a water heater. The style is classic Hop Inn — white-and-yellow palette, functional rather than decorative, no design statement. That said, cleanliness is what real reviewers consistently mention first, and many note it surpasses hotels in the 3–4 star category. Shared facilities include free Wi-Fi throughout, a 24-hour front desk, an elevator, and coin-operated washing machines in the lobby (useful for longer stays). Complimentary coffee and tea are available at the lobby counter before 11:00. There is no restaurant, no breakfast service, no swimming pool, and no fitness centre. Rooms do not have an in-room safe, and clothes hangars are limited to three — pack light or plan around this.

Service and staff — Guest reviews across both Booking.com and Trip.com repeatedly describe the staff as friendly, smiling, and genuinely helpful — a trait that shows up often enough to be a reliable characteristic rather than an isolated impression. Check-in runs from 14:00, check-out by 12:00. The Hop Inn chain has standardised procedures that make check-in fast and uncomplicated, which suits business travellers and those on tight schedules. One operational note worth knowing: hotel staff cannot call taxis on your behalf (chain policy) — you use the Grab app yourself. This is not a problem in practice as Grab coverage here is excellent, but it is worth knowing upfront if you expect a traditional concierge-style taxi service.

Honest guest feedback — what people actually say — with a score of 9.1/10 on Trip.com (252 reviews) and 9.2/10 on Booking.com (624 reviews), this is one of the highest-scoring budget hotels in Bangkok by volume of reviews. What guests praise: the BTS location is mentioned in nearly every positive review — "out the door and on the BTS in seconds" — followed by the room cleanliness, value for money, and friendly staff. Several reviews note the rooms are better maintained than many pricier options. What guests flag: no restaurant in the building and limited food options nearby, especially after 21:00 — you need Grab Food or a short walk. Rooms at the front of the building can pick up road noise from Krung Thonburi Road, so light sleepers should request a rear-facing room. No in-room safe and minimal storage space (three hangars) can feel tight with large luggage.

Price and value — rates start from about ฿700–800/night in the low-to-mid season (March–October), rising to roughly ฿1,000–1,200 during peak months (November–February) and Bangkok public holidays. For a hotel with a BTS station directly attached, a 9.1 review score, and 120 clean, consistently maintained rooms, that pricing is exceptional for central Bangkok. Comparable Silom or Sathon hotels with BTS access typically charge ฿1,500–2,500 per night at the 3-star tier. The trade-off is clear: you are paying budget price and getting budget amenities — no breakfast, no pool, limited storage. If those trade-offs work for your trip, the value proposition here is hard to beat.

Bottom line — HOP INN Bangkok Krung Thonburi Station does a very specific thing very well: it puts you on the BTS, in a clean room, for under ฿1,000 a night, on Bangkok's characterful Thonburi west side. The 9.1/10 score from 600+ real guests confirms this consistently delivers on its promise. Go in with clear expectations — no breakfast, no pool, limited storage — and you will leave satisfied. If any of those missing amenities matter to you, the honest answer is to budget upward to a 3-star property. But if the BTS, a clean bed, and Bangkok's best budget value are what you are after, this is the right call in this neighbourhood.

honestSummary: HOP INN Krung Thonburi Station is the right choice if you want a clean room with the BTS directly outside, for under ฿1,000 a night in Bangkok — scored 9.1 from 600+ real guests, outstanding location, consistent chain standards. Be clear-eyed: there is no breakfast, no restaurant, no pool, no in-room safe, and rooms are compact. If those trade-offs fit your trip, the value here is genuinely hard to beat in Bangkok.

tips.title: Take the Gold Line BTS to ICONSIAM — skip Grab entirely
tips.body: From BTS Krung Thonburi station, the Gold Line (Monorail) departs every 10–15 minutes to Klong San and ICONSIAM. Fare is ฿15–25 and the ride takes 5–8 minutes. It beats a Grab in rush-hour traffic by a wide margin and arrives at ICONSIAM's own station.

tips.title: Request a rear-facing room at check-in if noise bothers you
tips.body: Krung Thonburi Road is a busy arterial road, and front rooms pick up some traffic noise through the evening. Ask for a room at the back of the building or a higher floor when you check in — the front desk generally accommodates this request when availability allows.

tips.title: Breakfast: street food on Krung Thonburi Road or one BTS stop away
tips.body: The hotel has no breakfast service. Krung Thonburi Road has rice congee shops (khao tom), coffee stalls, and morning market vendors open from early. Alternatively, take the BTS one stop to Krung Thonburi for more varied options, or order Grab Food delivery straight to the lobby.

tips.title: Book early for November–February peak season
tips.body: Bangkok's cool-season peak (November–February) sees this hotel fill up fast, especially among international travellers who discover the BTS location. Rates can rise to ฿1,000–1,200 and popular room types sell out. Book on Agoda or Trip.com in advance and select Free Cancellation for flexibility.

faqTitle: FAQ — HOP INN Bangkok Krung Thonburi Station

faq.q: Is HOP INN Krung Thonburi Station actually next to the BTS?
faq.a: Yes — BTS Krung Thonburi station (Green Line Silom) is directly attached to the hotel building. Guests consistently describe it as a walk of under 30 seconds to the station entrance. From Krung Thonburi station you can reach Silom (Chong Nonsi) in 1 stop, Sathon in 2 stops, and Saphan Taksin river pier in 3 stops. The Gold Line BTS also departs from Krung Thonburi to ICONSIAM.

faq.q: How do I get from the hotel to ICONSIAM?
faq.a: The easiest way is the Gold Line BTS (Monorail) from BTS Krung Thonburi station — trains every 10–15 minutes, ฿15–25 fare, arrives at ICONSIAM's own station in 5–8 minutes. Alternatively, a Grab ride is approximately 5–8 minutes covering 1.6 km, though it will take longer during peak traffic hours.

faq.q: Does HOP INN Krung Thonburi Station serve breakfast?
faq.a: No. There is no breakfast service and no restaurant in the hotel. Complimentary coffee and tea are available at the lobby counter before 11:00. For breakfast, Krung Thonburi Road has street vendors and rice congee shops open from early morning, or take the BTS one stop inward to find more dining options.

faq.q: Is free parking available at HOP INN Krung Thonburi Station?
faq.a: Yes — free private parking is provided for hotel guests on site. No reservation is required; drive up and park on arrival. This is a genuine advantage on the Thonburi side of Bangkok where many visitors arrive by car before switching to BTS.

faq.q: What is the room rate at HOP INN Krung Thonburi Station?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿700–800 per night for a Standard Double during low-to-mid season (March–October). During peak months (November–February) and Bangkok public holidays, prices typically rise to ฿1,000–1,200. Book on Agoda or Trip.com in advance and choose Free Cancellation for maximum flexibility.
